>My audiologist said that my hearing loss would benefit from the Intent 1’s full use of its dual chips as opposed to partial use in the Intent 2.

The oticon Intent does NOT have dual chips. Your audi is thinking of the Phonak Sphere, or Starkey.

The Intent uses DNN and AI to achieve it's Speech in noise settings, with a lot of customization for the audi to program using the single onboard Sirius processor.

TBH, most users are fine with the Intent 2.

Yeah, Easy Line is the Sennheiser app, there's not a different one, but you are right that the pre-programmed the ones are very very basic. My audiologist added a couple more for me that were specific to settings ("programs") I wanted on my hearing aids, and she also made some adjustments to at least one of those basic programs that's also in the app to customize it a little more for what I was saying about hearing and not hearing sound around me. I think it was the restaurant setting.


My preference has always been to just manually reach up to my hearing aid and change programs, but I find that this button, and same thing with the phonak button when I tried that  recent one, a little bit unwieldy. 


What is important is that she do custom programs for you on your hearing aids, and then if the button is confusing or if you just prefer using the app anyhow, have her put those on the app
bonus points if you have a dead metal cuff and chain earring so your hearing aid is physically attached to you

Yes, since your audiologist did not show you what different sounds fall in different ones of those ranges, look online. Male and female voices are in different areas, vowels and consonants too, so you might find it lines up with the things you have difficulty with. Or, your audiogram and that info could show you the things you are not hearing well that you may *not* be aware of.

More important than that, the Costco audiologists I've had really know their stuff in terms of making adjustments. I just returned a $4,000 pair of hearing aids, actually $5,500 before my health insurance paid their $1,500. Great brand, I've had them before, but the audiologist was unable to program them correctly even with the sales rep also coming in and trying it twice, that rep had been in the field for many years.


I literally could not comprehend people talking to me even though I could with my old hearing aids. So I just saved $2,500, it is basically the same manufacturer and same model, but the Costco audiologist who I've been going to for years quickly program them and will make a tweak but honestly they're fantastic.
